cai-thia-xao-nam-dong-co.name: Stir-Fried Bok Choy with Shiitake Mushrooms
cai-thia-xao-nam-dong-co.serving_basis: One plate of vegetables for four people at a family meal.
cai-thia-xao-nam-dong-co.description: Crisp green bok choy pairs with fragrant shiitake mushrooms in a gently savory vegetarian glaze. This simple vegetable dish goes well with steamed rice and a braised main.
cai-thia-xao-nam-dong-co.finished_dish: The bok choy is just tender with a little bite, the mushrooms are soft and fragrant, and a light glossy sauce coats the vegetables.
cai-thia-xao-nam-dong-co.serving: Arrange on a plate while hot, spoon the mushrooms and sauce over the bok choy, and serve with steamed rice.
tips: If using dried shiitake, soak until soft and drain before cooking.
Stir-fry the bok choy over high heat and stop as soon as the stalks soften so they do not release excess water.
Use vegan oyster sauce and leek to keep the dish fully vegetarian.
cai-thia-xao-nam-dong-co.image_alt: Green bok choy stir-fried with shiitake mushrooms in a light vegetarian sauce on a ceramic plate.
cai-thia-xao-nam-dong-co.time_note: About 25 minutes; stir-fry briefly to keep the bok choy green and crisp.

ingredients.name: Bok choy
ingredients.notes: Separate the stalks, rinse well and drain.

ingredients.name: Fresh shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim tough stems; score the caps lightly if desired.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Rinse and thinly slice.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a variety suitable for vegetarian cooking.

ingredients.name: Vegan oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the brand.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Divide between the mushrooms and bok choy.

ingredients.name: Sesame oil
ingredients.notes: Add at the end for aroma.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Mix with cool water to prevent lumps.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the sauce.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the sauce and starch slurry.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle in at the end.

preparation_steps: Separate the bok choy into bite-size stalks, rinse and drain. Trim the shiitake stems and halve any large mushrooms.
Stir the soy sauce, vegan oyster sauce, sugar, tapioca starch and water together in a small bowl until smooth.
cooking_steps: Heat half the oil and saute the leek until fragrant. Add the mushrooms and stir-fry for about 2 minutes. Add part of the sauce, toss to coat, then transfer the mushrooms to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, raise the heat and stir-fry the bok choy for 2–3 minutes, until the stalks are just tender.
Return the mushrooms to the pan. Pour in the remaining sauce and toss gently until lightly thickened. Turn off the heat, finish with sesame oil and pepper, and serve hot.

dau-hu-xao-gia.name: Tofu Stir-Fried with Bean Sprouts
aliases: Vietnamese Tofu and Bean Sprout Stir-Fry
Vegetarian Tofu with Bean Sprouts and Chives
dau-hu-xao-gia.serving_basis: One plate of tofu and bean sprouts for four people with rice.
dau-hu-xao-gia.description: Lightly golden tofu is quickly tossed with crisp bean sprouts, green chives and a little soy sauce. It is an everyday vegetarian dish made with affordable, easy-to-find ingredients.
dau-hu-xao-gia.finished_dish: The tofu pieces hold their shape with lightly golden surfaces; the sprouts are just cooked and crisp, with no pooled liquid on the plate.
dau-hu-xao-gia.serving: Serve immediately while hot with steamed rice; it also pairs well with a bowl of vegetable soup.
tips: Pat the tofu dry before pan-frying to reduce splatter and help it brown evenly.
Drain the bean sprouts thoroughly, use high heat and stir-fry them briefly.
For a Buddhist vegetarian diet that avoids pungent aromatics, omit the garlic and adjust the soy sauce.
dau-hu-xao-gia.image_alt: Golden tofu stir-fried with crisp bean sprouts, green chives and tomato on a ceramic plate.
dau-hu-xao-gia.time_note: About 22 minutes; stir-fry the bean sprouts briefly to retain their crispness.

ingredients.name: Firm white tofu
ingredients.notes: Choose a firm block that is easy to pan-fry.

ingredients.name: Mung bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Remove loose bean skins, rinse and drain thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Chinese chives
ingredients.notes: Cut into 3 cm lengths.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: Cut into wedges; omit for a drier stir-fry.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a variety suitable for vegetarian cooking.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the product.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Softens the savory flavor.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the bean sprouts lightly.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Add to taste.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Finely chopped; omit for diets that avoid the five pungent aromatics.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Divide between pan-frying the tofu and stir-frying the vegetables.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Mix with the soy sauce and seasonings.

preparation_steps: Rinse the tofu gently, pat it dry and cut it into bite-size cubes. Rinse the bean sprouts, remove loose skins and drain well; cut the chives and tomato.
Mix the soy sauce, vegetarian seasoning powder, sugar, pepper and water until dissolved. Keep the mixture ready for quick seasoning.
cooking_steps: Heat most of the oil over medium heat. Pan-fry the tofu until lightly golden on each side, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and saute the garlic, if using. Add the tomato and stir briefly until just softened.
Raise the heat, add the bean sprouts and stir-fry for about a minute. Add the tofu and seasoning mixture; toss gently, add the chives, stir for about 20 seconds and turn off the heat.

canh-rong-bien-dau-hu-chay.name: Vegetarian Seaweed and Tofu Soup
aliases: Vegetarian Seaweed, Mushroom and Tofu Soup
canh-rong-bien-dau-hu-chay.serving_basis: One light pot of vegetarian soup for four people.
canh-rong-bien-dau-hu-chay.description: Seaweed, soft tofu and mushrooms simmer in a light vegetable broth. Ginger and leek add fragrance, making this a gentle soup for a vegetarian family meal.
canh-rong-bien-dau-hu-chay.finished_dish: The broth is clear and mild, with soft tofu and just-tender vegetables; the seaweed remains intact rather than overcooked.
canh-rong-bien-dau-hu-chay.serving: Ladle into a bowl while hot, garnish with cilantro and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Soak the dried seaweed only until expanded, then rinse it well.
Add the seaweed near the end and simmer only a few minutes so it keeps its texture.
Use vegetarian seasoning or vegetable stock and do not add fish sauce.
canh-rong-bien-dau-hu-chay.image_alt: A bowl of vegetarian seaweed soup with soft tofu and enoki mushrooms in vegetable broth.
canh-rong-bien-dau-hu-chay.time_note: About 35 minutes, including the time to simmer the vegetables and finish the soup.

ingredients.name: Dried seaweed
ingredients.notes: Soak until expanded, rinse and cut into bite-size lengths.

ingredients.name: Soft tofu
ingredients.notes: Cut into bite-size cubes and handle gently.

ingredients.name: Enoki mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the base, rinse briefly and drain.

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Rinse and halve larger mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into thin slices.

ingredients.name: Daikon
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Cut into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Add gradually and taste before adding more.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the broth.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional; balances the natural sweetness of the vegetables.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sauteing the leek.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: May be partly replaced with vegetable stock.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse, chop and sprinkle on top before serving.

preparation_steps: Soak the seaweed for about 15 minutes until expanded, rinse and drain. Cut the tofu into cubes; prepare the mushrooms, carrot, daikon, leek and ginger.
Keep the mushrooms and firm vegetables separate; cut the enoki into short lengths. Measure the vegetarian seasoning powder, salt and sugar.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot and saute the leek until fragrant. Add the straw mushrooms and daikon, stir gently, then add the water. Simmer gently for about 10 minutes to draw out their flavor.
Add the carrot and enoki and cook for a few minutes. Season with vegetarian seasoning powder, salt and a little sugar, then add the tofu and keep the heat low so it does not break apart.
Add the seaweed and ginger and simmer for 2–3 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning, turn off the heat, sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot.

bap-cai-cuon-chay.name: Vegetarian Cabbage Rolls
aliases: Cabbage Rolls with Mushrooms and Vegetables
bap-cai-cuon-chay.serving_basis: About eight vegetable rolls for four people as a side dish.
bap-cai-cuon-chay.description: Soft cabbage leaves wrap a fragrant filling of carrot, bamboo shoots and enoki mushrooms. The rolls are steamed and finished with a lightly thickened vegetable sauce for an easy vegetarian addition to the family table.
bap-cai-cuon-chay.finished_dish: The cabbage rolls hold their shape, the vegetable filling is tender with a little bite, and the clear sauce is lightly thickened without masking the vegetables.
bap-cai-cuon-chay.serving: Arrange the rolls on a plate, spoon over the warm sauce and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Blanch the cabbage leaves just until pliable and drain them before filling so they do not tear.
Cook the filling only until the vegetables are just tender; excess liquid can loosen the rolls.
Mix the cornstarch with cool water before adding it to the sauce to prevent lumps.
bap-cai-cuon-chay.image_alt: Steamed cabbage rolls filled with carrot, bamboo shoots and enoki mushrooms, topped with a light vegetarian sauce.
bap-cai-cuon-chay.time_note: About 45 minutes, including preparation, filling, rolling and steaming.

ingredients.name: White cabbage
ingredients.notes: Separate the large leaves, rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Enoki mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the base, rinse briefly and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into short thin strips.

ingredients.name: Parboiled bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Use pre-cooked shoots and cut into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Finely chop for the filling.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the filling and sauce.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Divide between the filling and sauce.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the filling.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.notes: Mix with cool water to make a lightly thickened sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For stir-frying the filling.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use part to blanch leaves and the rest for the sauce.

preparation_steps: Carefully separate the cabbage leaves, trim some of the thick ribs, rinse and blanch briefly in boiling water until pliable. Lift out and drain.
Cut the carrot, bamboo shoots and enoki into thin strips. Mix the vegetarian fish sauce, part of the seasoning powder and pepper for the filling.
cooking_steps: Saute the leek in hot oil. Add the carrot and bamboo shoots and stir for a few minutes. Add the enoki, season and cook until just tender; let the filling cool slightly.
Place a portion of filling in the middle of each cabbage leaf. Fold in both sides and roll neatly; set each roll seam-side down to hold its shape.

Steam the rolls for 7–8 minutes until the leaves are tender. Meanwhile, simmer the remaining water with the rest of the seasoning and vegetarian fish sauce. Stir in the cornstarch slurry until the sauce is lightly thickened.
Arrange the rolls on a plate, spoon over the warm sauce and serve immediately.

rau-den-luoc-cham-tuong.name: Boiled Amaranth Greens with Soy Dipping Sauce
aliases: Boiled Red Amaranth with Soy Sauce
rau-den-luoc-cham-tuong.serving_basis: One plate of greens with a small bowl of soy sauce for four people.
rau-den-luoc-cham-tuong.description: Tender boiled amaranth greens have a naturally mild sweetness and are served with a simple bowl of soy sauce. This familiar, unfussy vegetable dish suits a vegetarian meal or a light family dinner.
rau-den-luoc-cham-tuong.finished_dish: The stems are tender but intact and the leaves are not mushy; red amaranth keeps its natural pink-purple color after boiling.
rau-den-luoc-cham-tuong.serving: Arrange the greens on a plate, let excess water drain away and serve with a small bowl of soy sauce, warm or hot.
tips: Remove damaged leaves and tough stems, then rinse several times to remove grit.
Add the greens only after the water boils and cook until just tender; overcooking makes them limp.
Red amaranth may tint the cooking water a natural pink-purple color.
search_terms: boiled amaranth greens with soy sauce
rau-den-luoc-cham-tuong.image_alt: Tender boiled red amaranth greens on a ceramic plate with a small bowl of soy dipping sauce.
rau-den-luoc-cham-tuong.time_note: About 18 minutes; boil the greens for roughly 2–3 minutes after the water comes to a boil.

ingredients.name: Amaranth greens
ingredients.notes: Use red or green amaranth; remove damaged leaves and tough stems.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Add a small amount to the boiling water.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Optional; use a small amount in the boiling water.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Serve separately as a dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Enough to submerge the greens while boiling.

preparation_steps: Remove damaged leaves and fibrous stems, break the greens into bite-size lengths, rinse several times and drain.
Pour the soy sauce into a small bowl for dipping. If the greens are sandy, soak them briefly in clean water and rinse again.
cooking_steps: Bring the water to a boil with the salt and a little oil, if using. Add the amaranth only once the water is bubbling steadily.
Boil for about 2–3 minutes, turning the greens gently once. Lift out a stem to check; when just tender, remove the greens and let them drain.
Arrange the greens on a plate and serve with soy sauce. Do not leave them sitting in the hot water, or they will become overcooked.
